result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with mixed-use and residential buildings, featuring sidewalks on both sides and a stop-controlled intersection. While the narrow street width naturally limits vehicle speeds, the pedestrian infrastructure is dated, with faded crosswalk markings and a lack of visible ADA-compliant curb ramps.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The transverse crosswalk lines are significantly worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: There are no visible sloped transitions from the sidewalk to the street level, creating a barrier for people with mobility impairments.
hazards.location_in_image: Corners of the intersection in the foreground

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Replace faded transverse lines with continental-style high-visibility markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install ADA-compliant curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at all crossing points.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The street lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and clear lane markings. Narrow, cracked sidewalks and parked vehicles that obstruct sightlines create a hazardous environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated places for pedestrians to cross the street safely.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block the view between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Degraded sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is narrow and shows significant cracking, which could be a trip hazard.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-striped crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add bulb-outs at corners to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility by preventing parking too close to the intersection.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair and Widening
interventions.description: Repair the existing sidewalk and widen it where possible to provide a safer, more accessible walking path.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a sidewalk that terminates into a wide, unmarked asphalt area serving as a parking lot entrance or side street. There is a notable lack of pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or signals, creating a high-exposure environment for people walking.

There is a complete absence of marked pedestrian crossings, signals, or lane markings, which increases risk for those crossing the street. The roadway surface shows signs of degradation with visible cracking and patches.
